items.title: Eddie Miller and Pete Fountain Interview, 1970-01-09
items.q: Interviewer asks about 'you and Al Hurt' having a TV program; Interviewee responds about the logistics of such a program but does not describe a personal relationship with Al Hurt.

ctx.x: No, we're not going to tape it or anything. We couldn't anyway, unless we had permission through the union. And he records for command records, and I record for Decker, so we couldn't... All those people there, then, huh? Well, with the company, it's not between he and I. He and I have been good buddies for the last, I'd say, eight years.

Uh-huh. And I was wondering, too, Pete, how come, in other words, like you and Al Hurt, how come they don't give, well, have, say, somewhat like a television program here local with such great talent as you and Al?

Well, they were trying to get something like that going here, but it just wouldn't work out. I guess it's too expensive to come down here and do it. I see. It's cheaper to fly us up there to New York or California, or, like I said, Nashville's doing a lot of work. I'll be doing a lot of TV out of there soon. I see.
